However, it is unlikely by itself to change urgent management in this encounter given ongoing discussion of current breathlessness and reliever use.

safety_verdicts.content: If breathlessness worsens before seeing a doctor, patient should attend A&E.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated provides general safety-netting but does not specifically advise attending A&E if worsening before review.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to explicitly safety-net with instructions to attend A&E if breathlessness worsens can delay escalation during an asthma exacerbation, increasing the risk of deterioration without timely emergency care. This can adversely affect outcomes even if deterioration is not certain.

safety_verdicts.content: Using blue inhaler (salbutamol) currently every 4 hours and also morning and evening preventatively
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Conflicts with Gold which states blue inhaler use up to twice daily (hpi-003/med-002). Transcript supports max dosing advice (2–4 hourly) but not that the patient is 'currently every 4 hours' as a factual current-use pattern.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting that the patient is currently using salbutamol every 4 hours and preventatively may overstate reliever dependence, potentially prompting unnecessary escalation or misclassification of severity/control. While unlikely to cause major harm alone, it can meaningfully distort clinical interpretation and follow-up urgency.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies mild exacerbation (asm-001). Transcript describes 'small exacerbation' rather than mild-to-moderate; 'mild-to-moderate' overstates severity beyond Gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Labeling the exacerbation as mild-to-moderate instead of mild modestly overstates severity and could lead to slightly more aggressive management or increased patient anxiety. The difference is unlikely to directly cause injury in most cases.
